newsitem.title: CHINA: China launches military satellite - sources.
newsitem.headline: China launches military satellite - sources.

text.p: China has successfully launched a satellite for defence use, Chinese sources said on Sunday.
They said the satellite was launched last week but did not give details of its role or say what type of rocket was used.
"The satellite is for defence purposes," one of the sources told Reuters. "The launch was successful."
Other sources confirmed the launch's success but were equally tight-lipped about the mission's objectives.

The launch, which closely followed the blasting into orbit of a communications satellite this month, marked another milestone in China's drive to restore its reputation as a reliable provider of commercial satellite launch services.
China had been hit by a string of failures that badly tarnished its image over the past two years.
The mishaps sent insurance premiums soaring, effectively erasing China's advantages from its low launch prices.

In China's most spectacular failure, a Long March 3B rocket carrying a satellite for the global organisation Intelsat, veered off course and exploded in February last year. At least six people were killed and 57 injured on the ground.
In August last year, a U.S.-built communications satellite failed to reach proper orbit after its launch on a Long March 3 rocket.
China said last week its Dongfanghong-3 (East is Red) communications satellite, launched this month aboard a Long March 3A rocket, had been successfully moved into synchronous orbit.
That prompted public congratulations from China's State Council (cabinet) and the powerful Central Military Commission to those involved in the space programme.

China plans to launch its first domestically made geostationary weather satellite, the Fengyun-2, next month. That is expected to be followed by several commercial launches before the end of the year.
